title: Shahi Safed Murgh (Moonlight Murgh)
description: A rich North Indian white chicken curry made with a silky onion-almond-yogurt gravy, aromatic whole spices, white pepper, and kasuri methi. Mildly spiced, creamy, and perfect with naan or rice.

ingredients.item: olive oil or neutral cooking oil

steps: Boil the onions, almonds, and garlic cloves in enough water until the onions become completely soft, about 12–15 minutes.
Drain and allow the mixture to cool slightly.
Blend the onions, almonds, garlic, yogurt, coriander powder, a little salt, and a splash of water until completely smooth and creamy.
Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Add the minced garlic and sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until lightly golden and about halfway cooked, 5–6 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the green cardamom, black peppercorns, cloves, and cinnamon stick. Toast for about 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1–2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Pour in the prepared onion-almond gravy and cook over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring frequently until it thickens slightly.
Return the chicken and any accumulated juices to the pan.
Season with salt, white pepper powder, slit green chilies, and garam masala.
Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked and the gravy becomes rich and creamy. If it becomes too thick, add a little hot water.
When the oil begins to separate slightly around the edges, crush the Kasoori methi between your palms and stir it into the curry.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld.
notes: White onions are preferred because they produce a naturally pale, sweeter gravy.
Blanching the almonds removes any raw taste and creates a smoother texture.
Blend and strain the gravy for an ultra-silky restaurant-style finish.
For an even richer version, stir in 2–3 tablespoons of fresh cream during the final minute of cooking.
Do not overcook the chicken after adding it back to the gravy, as boneless thighs remain juiciest when just cooked through.
Serve with butter naan, garlic naan, tandoori roti, roomali roti, or steamed basmati rice.
